title: Map the Reachable Area (Flood Fill)
real_world_story: A cleaning robot starts in one room and must know how much floor area it can actually reach before walls and furniture block it. The coverage planner needs the count of every reachable free cell.

real_world_connection.input_represents: Floor map where 0 is cleanable floor and 1 is furniture or a wall
real_world_connection.algorithm_represents: Flooding outward from the dock to paint every reachable cell

problem_statement: Given an R x C grid of 0 (free) and 1 (wall) and a start cell (sr, sc), count how many free cells are reachable from the start using 4-directional moves through free cells only.
task: Return the number of reachable free cells including the start cell, or 0 if the start cell is a wall.
input_format: The first line contains two integers R and C. The next R lines each contain C integers (0 or 1). The final line contains two integers sr sc.
output_format: Print the count of reachable free cells.

examples.explanation: From (0,0) the robot can reach (0,0), (0,1), and (1,0). Walls block the rest.

expected_algorithm.name: Flood Fill
expected_algorithm.reason: Flood fill spreads from the start across connected free cells, which is exactly the reachable-area region.

hint: If the start is a wall, answer 0 immediately.
Use BFS/DFS from the start through free cells only.
Count every cell the first time you visit it.
real_world_takeaway: Flood fill maps the full region a robot or player can reach, which is essential for coverage and level validation.
